Source says only such minds can sound these truths even with much time and care; 'and then only with much time and care' makes time and care a condition and shifts the qualification.
replacement: This, then, is the subject on which it is most important for each of us to hold fixed ideas. Unhappily, it is also the subject on which it is hardest for each of us, left alone, to settle our opinions by the force of reason alone. Only minds unusually free from the ordinary anxieties of life, minds that are at once penetrating, subtle, and trained in thinking, can sound the depths of these most necessary truths, even with the help of much time and care. Indeed, we see that these philosophers are themselves almost always wrapped in uncertainties. At every step the natural light that illuminates their path grows dimmer and less secure. In spite of all their efforts, they have so far discovered only a small number of conflicting ideas, on which the human mind has been tossed about for thousands of years without getting a firmer grip on the truth or even finding anything new in its errors. Studies of this kind are far above the average capacity of people. And even if most of mankind were capable of such pursuits, it is clear that they would still lack the leisure to pursue them. Fixed ideas of God and of human nature are indispensable to the daily conduct of people’s lives, but the conduct of their lives prevents them from acquiring such ideas.
